findings.title: Hidden-wallet repetition encoding leaves the first owned password copy unwiped on refusal
findings.evidence: AUD-011-harnesses/browser/secret-refusals.mjs; local secret-refusals.log exits 1 with first-copy wipe assertion.
findings.reproduction: Obtain an ordinary ready hidden-wallet session. Call session.open({password:'synthetic-test', passwordRepeat:'\uD800'}). requireRepetition accepts both string types. The first encodeSecret allocates an owned Uint8Array; the second rejects malformed UTF-16 with INVALID_PASSWORD_TEXT. Instrument TextEncoder to retain that first array and observe nonzero bytes after rejection.
findings.expected: Every package-owned secret buffer is zeroed on all fallible request-construction paths, without changing caller-owned buffers.
findings.observed: Object-literal evaluation allocates the password before repetition encoding. The exception occurs before assignment of message and before sendRequest/wipeSecrets, so the first allocation has no cleanup owner.
findings.impact: Local residual-memory lifetime defect on malformed repeated input. No network disclosure, secret theft, access from another process, or guaranteed persistence beyond garbage collection was demonstrated. Caller-owned strings cannot be securely wiped by JavaScript regardless.
findings.recommendedFix: Construct the request incrementally inside a cleanup guard, using the same guarded secret-request pattern as other public operations. Wipe all already allocated buffers if any subsequent encoding fails.
findings.requiredVerification: Add public hidden-session regression for malformed repetition, second-buffer allocation failure and request-send failure; assert owned first copies are zeroed, caller buffers preserved, no worker request sent, and a subsequent valid open succeeds.
findings.challenge: Independent package reviewer accepted the unchanged public method reproduction. Mock worker/startup bypass only establish session readiness; they do not replace the encoding path or demonstrate real browser startup.
findings.historicalContext: AUD-009-SEC001 affected passwords.js and wallet.js and remains historically verified by AUD-010. This is a new hidden-session occurrence introduced by replacing equality-checking requireSamePassword with type-only requireRepetition.

findings.title: CLI password-size refusals discard and duplicate library-owned error messages
findings.evidence: AUD-011-harnesses/dry-probe.mjs; local dry-probe.log records both duplicates and exits 1. Exact source traces show map_err(|_|...) reconstruction.
findings.reproduction: Inspect PasswordRecipe::words/characters: both author InvalidPasswordSize text. CLI run/run_characters call these constructors but discard their errors and rebuild 'Choose between 1 and {MOST_*} words/characters'. The limits are imported, but the refusal wording has two owners.
findings.expected: The library owns the rule/refusal once; front ends preserve its error and only translate capitalization, punctuation and exit codes through the existing adapter.
findings.observed: Two CLI refusal branches independently format messages already returned by the library. This conflicts with the explicitly requested message-level DRY rule and qualifies the release note's absolute single-source claim.
findings.impact: Maintainability/documentation-contract defect, not an observed wrong bound or runtime security failure. Future error changes can diverge; present constants agree.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the existing MhfeError-to-Failure/refused adapter instead of rebuilding those messages; keep contextual CLI guidance separate from the shared error.
findings.requiredVerification: CLI out-of-range word and character counts retain the library message after normal display translation, return exit2 before generation, and valid boundary sizes still work. Rerun semantic source review; the lexical probe alone is not exhaustive.
findings.challenge: Coordinator verified the exact library/CLI traces. Generated-password display paths have distinct private-screen/confirmation lifetimes and are not an additional finding.

findings.title: API documentation understates the native self-test component count
findings.evidence: AUD-011-harnesses/doc-count.mjs reproduces 23 versus 24 and exits 1; native composition assertions pass in rust-tests.
findings.reproduction: Compare the native(random) component count at docs/API.md:396 with NATIVE_IDS and native composition in src/self_check/sets.rs.
findings.expected: Published self-test inventory agrees with the executed composition.
findings.observed: The documentation says 23 parts; the native set contains 24 including ContainerSearchCheck.
findings.impact: Stale factual count only. No missing container-search coverage or wrong self-test result was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct or remove the fragile literal count; preferably check published inventory against composition metadata.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify documentation inventory and count against the native set, and keep the native composition tests passing.
findings.challenge: Independent package reviewer confirmed the discrepancy and its bounded non-security impact.

architectureGroups: A - check/password/eligibility rules

ContainerFacts/Suite own lengths and capabilities; Reference::identifies_wallet and rehearsal::refuse_impossible own reference applicability; PasswordReview and wallet_check repetition validators are shared.
src/container.rs; src/suite.rs; src/rehearsal.rs:179,279; src/check_word.rs; src/wallet_check.rs:126
JS early-refusal limits remain a documented guarded fast-path copy, not literally one source.
B - lengths and phrase reading

packing defines state/short lengths; WordCount/PhraseLength and phrase helpers own mappings/normalization; repair::ContainerReading reused by ContainerSearch; LengthDetection owns ambiguity decisions.
src/packing.rs; src/phrase.rs; src/repair.rs; src/search.rs:85; src/detection.rs:24
Search checksum packing is an explicit fast path with equivalence tests; independent known-answer constants must not be deduplicated into the implementation under test.

RecoveredForCheck::compare and shared recovery serve check callers; search wallet/own-check modes reuse recover_each; vector writer delegates encryption.
src/rehearsal.rs:201,262; src/search.rs:194; src/vectors.rs
Reference reconstruction to change address limits is an optional composition improvement, not a confirmed wrong result.
D - error/JSON/formatting helpers
SelfCheckReport/failure_message own failure text; shared fingerprint formatting/callback adapters and MhfeError supply normal output.
src/self_check.rs:205; src/wallet.rs; src/wasm_api/mod.rs; src/error.rs
Password-size text still duplicated: ARC001.
E - browser scaffolding
ModuleWorker, PackageCheck, OperationSlot and WorkerJob are composed by module classes; no deep inheritance or repeated worker lifecycle needed.
web/runtime.js; web/client.js; web/repair.js; web/passwords.js; web/wallet.js
Secret-field copies explain worker import constraints and have equality gates. Hidden-session special path still lacks cleanup: SEC001.
F - CLI questions/rendering/retry
phrase_length, choice, check::WalletReference, container_repair, encrypt/made_password, exit::refused and style::retry consolidate shared prompts and adapters.
src/bin/mhfe/phrase_length.rs; choice.rs; check.rs; container_repair.rs; made_password.rs; exit.rs; style.rs
Prompt-specific continuations and distinct output destinations are not automatically duplicate domain rules.
limitations: No full-size Argon2 vector replays or ignored full-size tests; metadata/vector hashes are not a full-cost replay.
No canonical Docker rebuild, fresh browser WASM rebuild, release archive generation/signature verification, paid GitHub Actions or current Windows/macOS execution.
Existing browser artifact relationship is supported by script/source equality, stamp/manifest checks and dep-info timestamps, not canonical reproducibility proof.
No exhaustive upstream dependency audit, fresh external advisory query or independent cryptographic certification.
No end-to-end integration audit of the surrounding Deriver: browser package is tested as a package, not the external page's field-level workflows.
The new secret-copy probe uses a mock ready worker and bypasses startup to isolate unchanged request encoding; real browser execution is separate evidence.
The DRY probe is an exact source witness of two named copies, not a generic clone detector or proof of absence of other duplicates.
Audit artifacts only were edited; generated target outputs may change when compiling. No commit/push/tag/release authorized.
Terminal self-test sections may overlap browser CPU-only phrase drawing; timings are not controlled performance measurements.
Original debug terminal suite timed out in two-word enumeration after 120 seconds. The unchanged scenario and remaining tail passed on the optimized build; the entire debug suite was not rerun.
principles: SRP
Library owns encryption, repair, password and wallet rules; front ends adapt. No further mandatory module split identified.
OCP
Variants/traits carry most changeable behavior; optional Reference limit-copy helper can reduce caller coupling.
LSP
Native/browser Argon2 and worker contracts checked by KATs and package parity; no proven contract violation.
ISP
Small engine/randomness/progress interfaces and four focused browser classes.
DIP
Host services injected via traits/callbacks; CLI is not the domain implementation.
DRY
Two duplicated error message constructions remain (ARC001). Documented fast-path/import-boundary copies have equality checks.
Encapsulation
Rust private data/owned secret types and JS composition are appropriate; one exceptional allocation cleanup gap (SEC001).
Composition
ModuleWorker/PackageCheck/OperationSlot/WorkerJob and Rust service composition avoid deep inheritance.
Interfaces
Engine/progress/worker boundaries are narrow and testable.
Delegation
ContainerFacts/Suite/Reference/LengthDetection answer their own capabilities rather than callers re-deciding word counts.
recommendations: Optional: let Reference own adjustment of address-search limits instead of reconstructing its variants in search::decoy_reference.
Optional: add explicit native/browser progress-callback timing parity tests if immediate first-candidate cancellation is a documented requirement. No such violated guarantee was established.
Do not mechanically wrap pure helper functions or independent test vectors in additional classes. Cohesion and ownership, not class count, are the audit criteria.

environment.argon2Budget: No full-size operational encryption/replays. Browser package KAT memory up to 256 MiB; operational tests use 256 KiB/one pass. CLI terminal flows refuse before operational Argon2; its self-test portions run actual native KATs. Native build/PTY checks overlap the CPU-heavy browser phrase search, so timing is not a benchmark.

assessment: The refactor is structurally in the right direction: most reported rule copies are consolidated into domain owners and focused browser modules; adding more classes mechanically is not required. Three low, nonblocking confirmed findings remain. No critical/high/medium defect was confirmed by this bounded audit. This is not release acceptance or proof of absence of further defects.

runtimeSummary: CLI/browser parity passed. The original debug terminal run passed its input/private-screen/repair/refusal cases but stopped at the 120-second two-missing-word enumeration wait (exact assertion retained in local cli-terminal.log). A freshly checked optimized build passed that identical search scenario and the previously unreached usage/script/startup/self-test/fault-injection tail through terminal-search.py, with unchanged assertions/timeouts. No claim of an uninterrupted all-green debug terminal suite is made. The scoped pass supports a build-profile timing limitation, not a proven production UI defect. Real Chromium 153.0.8010.12 and Firefox 155.0 passed all four module classes in standard file and fast cross-origin-isolated localhost modes, with real Blob workers, transfer/cancel/error/session/startup tests and no stray requests. Operational encryption uses the declared reduced cost, not a full-size browser acceptance test.
